title: Android Workbench Bring-Up, Runtime Validation, and Repository-Access Boundary

preflight.note: Opened to turn the existing Tauri Workbench (WI055/WI058) into a real Android-runnable application on the Dell Precision's actual Android SDK/emulator environment, exercise the compact/mobile IA WI058 designed (which had Android runtime evidence explicitly unexecuted), and classify the production Android repository-access boundary rather than silently redesigning RepoPact's repository model to appear Android-supported. Does not reopen WI058 or WI059.

acceptance_criteria.text: Inventory the Precision's actual Android environment before installing or modifying anything (tauri info, java -version, adb version/devices, rustup Android targets, ANDROID_HOME/ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/JAVA_HOME/NDK, Android Studio, SDK platform/build-tools/platform-tools/NDK versions, attached emulator/device Android version/API/ABI/model). Install only missing components actually required; no unrelated upgrades.

Record an architecture baseline in WI060 (informed by completed WI055, WI057, WI058, WI059 and Decision 0041) before modifying code: the desktop crate has src/main.rs only with no mobile lib target; select_repository uses blocking_pick_folder()/into_path(); Tauri's Android dialog cannot select folders; Android file selection yields content URIs, not a recursive repository root; DesktopService consumes a filesystem directory; NativeGitRunner invokes an external git binary Android cannot assume exists; RepoPact can still operate on exported/non-Git trees since Git topology queries are gated on .git presence; WI058's mobile IA had Android runtime evidence explicitly unexecuted. Do not claim WI058 already solved Android production repository selection.

Convert the Tauri desktop crate to the standard shared desktop/mobile shape: add a [lib] target (crate-type staticlib/cdylib/rlib), move the shared builder/app body into src/lib.rs, expose #[cfg_attr(mobile, tauri::mobile_entry_point)] pub fn run(), keep src/main.rs as a thin desktop entry point (preserving the Windows subsystem attribute), with no duplicated command registration. Windows Tauri build and existing tests must pass unchanged after this refactor before continuing.

Initialize the Android project using the installed Tauri CLI (tauri android init), not hand-written Gradle scaffolding, generating the project under src-tauri/gen/android and preserving the existing identifier com.forgewirelabs.repopact.workbench.

Keep Tauri security narrow on Android: withGlobalTauri stays false, local packaged frontend only, CSP preserved unless demonstrably necessary to change, no generic frontend filesystem/shell/process authority granted, the existing workbench-commands IPC permission remains the authority surface (any Android-specific capability file stays as narrow as the desktop one rather than core:default or a broad mobile permission set), and no broad storage/shell/process/internet Android permissions requested merely for bring-up convenience.

Platform-gate select_repository: desktop keeps the native folder picker; Android must not call blocking_pick_folder() or convert a content:// URI into a path. A normal Android production build returns a typed explicit error (e.g. repository.mobile-selection-unavailable) when no mobile repository-acquisition architecture exists, without requesting legacy broad storage permissions, hard-coding /sdcard/..., faking a path from a content URI, or adding an unrestricted open_repository(path) command.

Create a controlled, debug-only, app-private Android validation-repository mechanism (Git-free exported/representative RepoPact tree staged into the debug app's private files directory via adb/run-as or an equivalently scoped debug mechanism), gated by an explicit Cargo feature or tightly scoped cfg(all(target_os = "android", debug_assertions)) path, unavailable from normal production Android authority, and not confused with solving production repository selection. Document exactly how the tree is staged and opened.

Prove the Android runtime does not depend on Git for the exported app-private tree: no attempted git process launch on open/navigation of a .git-free tree, watcher state reported truthfully (Unavailable if the platform watcher backend does not work, rather than a false live-watching claim or a failed repository open).

Produce a reproducible Android debug build, install and launch it on the actual available Android target (physical device preferred over creating a new emulator; use the existing emulator if no physical device is available) via Tauri's Android command or adb, reaching the Workbench UI (not merely successful Gradle compilation). Record APK/package/ABI/device details and scoped adb logcat for startup and repository open.

Validate the compact/mobile IA on-device against the app-private repository: Dashboard, Work, Decisions, Evidence, Graph, Validation, Analysis, Settings; touch targets, secondary tabs, paging, search, drawer navigation, list-to-detail flows, compact Graph representation; no page-wide horizontal scrolling in ordinary phone portrait use, no essential hover/right-click interaction, no impractical tiny nested scroll regions.

Implement and prove Android system Back correctly, preferring the official @tauri-apps/api Android onBackButtonPress API over custom Kotlin if available: unwind order is close an open compact nav drawer, then leave a detail view and restore list state, then dismiss other transient presentation state, only then fall through to normal Android Back/exit. Preserve selected tab/query/pager context across that unwind. Add executable frontend tests for the state-machine portion and prove actual device Back/gesture behavior manually (not via browser URL history unless it genuinely represents that state).

Validate orientation and lifecycle on-device: rotate portrait to landscape and back without resetting the active repository session, selected primary page, secondary tab, list/search/pager context, or detail/list state; background and resume the app and record whether the native session survives and the UI returns coherently. Do not claim process-death recovery unless explicitly tested and implemented.

Validate safe-area and virtual-keyboard behavior on the actual Android WebView: top/bottom system UI, gesture/navigation area, dialogs/panels, pager controls; open a mutation/create/edit form, focus text inputs, show the IME, and prove the relevant field and submit/review controls remain reachable without broken nested scrolling. Diagnose actual env(safe-area-inset-*) behavior on-device before applying any workaround.

Exercise real Rust-backed operations on-device beyond presentation: repository overview, validation, work lists/details, decision/evidence detail, graph, analysis against the app-private validation repository; then use a disposable/scratch copy to exercise at least one Rust-owned mutation plan/review/apply path and verify post-state validation, confirming opaque plan handles and stale-plan semantics remain native-owned. Never mutate the canonical development checkout from the device.

Capture durable Android evidence: representative portrait/landscape screenshots (or recorded artifact hashes/paths per RepoPact conventions if binary commits are inappropriate), scoped logcat for startup/repository-open/Back/mutation-apply, and explicit operator confirmation for touch/gesture behavior that cannot be inferred from logs. Never claim a gesture passed without actual device interaction.

Explicitly decide and record the production Android repository-access boundary. If Tauri's dialog plugin cannot supply a repository directory on Android and a system Git binary cannot be assumed, create a new proposed follow-up work item (e.g. WI061, 'Mobile Repository Acquisition, App-Private Workspace, and Git Strategy') comparing app-private import/export, SAF ACTION_OPEN_DOCUMENT_TREE plus a safe recursive-copy layer, archive import, embedded Git/libgit2/gix, and remote clone/sync approaches, without choosing or implementing that architecture under WI060.

Closeout requires both Android evidence and a green Windows non-regression pass: Rust workspace (including the lib.rs refactor rebuilt for Windows Tauri), relevant Python/conformance/WI050 checks, frontend typecheck/tests/build, WI057 Git-count/cache tests, Tauri security tests, canonical repopact validate, dashboard canonicality, and frozen-surface checks. Do not close WI060 merely because tauri android build succeeds; the application must actually launch and be exercised on Android, and production Android repository selection must not be claimed complete if only the validation fixture can be opened.
